name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Focused on playback loading speed and fair bandwidth sharing. Streamed items now carry their source bitrate from the sync itself, so this server can tell up front whether a remote file already fits under a WAN cap and direct-play it instead of always forcing a remux - the single biggest source of slow-to-start playback until now. That check used to be duplicated (and could disagree with itself) in three different places; it's now one shared decision (FederationLibraryManager.IsWanCappedTranscode) used everywhere.

Also new: an optional automatic upload budget. Turn it on and the plugin divides your configured upload capacity across however many federated streams are currently active, so one viewer doesn't stutter because five friends started watching at once, and a single viewer isn't throttled to a five-way split when they're the only one watching. Adjusts every couple of minutes as sessions come and go.

The standalone admin page (Plugins/Federation/App) got a redesign to go with it: a real sidebar, a Library tab with a poster-grid preview of what's actually being federated, per-server streaming/WAN settings editable inline, and mappings you can enable, disable, or remove without touching the main config page.

201 tests (up from 187).
